pr_title: Bluetooth: Host: Add generic pairing query callback
pr_body:
Similar to pairing_confirm this callback is called each
time a peer requests pairing, but for all types of
pairings, except SSP. The pairing req/rsp information is
passed as a parameter so the application can decide
wheter to accept or reject the pairing.

Fixes: #21036

Signed-off-by: Martin Rieva <mrrv@demant.com>
pr_comments: @demantmrrv please rebase correctly so that you don't include unrelated commits

**All checks are passing now.**



*Tip: The bot edits this comment instead of posting a new one, so you can check the comment's history to see earlier messages.*
Built and tested OK without Kconfig flag and with Kconfig flag with app returning either zero or non-zero value in callback.

@demantmrrv we had a short chat with @aescolar and @joerchan with the following concensus:

 - Rename `bt_conn_pairing_info` to `bt_conn_pairing_feat` since this "information" is called "features" in the spec (as in "Pairing Feature Exchange"). The parameter name would then just be `feat`.
 - Rename the callback to `pairing_accept` (it's for asking the application if the given pairing features can be accepted)
 - Rename the Kconfig variable to `BT_SMP_USER_PAIRING_ACCEPT` (having "user" in there is clearer in that it's about enabling something extra for the user to accept, rather than looking like some global boolean allow/deny option)
@jhedberg About the latter bullet; the "user" ie. person, should not be informed about this as it is a synchronous call. If "user" indicates the application, no worries then.

> @jhedberg About the latter bullet; the "user" ie. person, should not be informed about this as it is a synchronous call. If "user" indicates the application, no worries then.

It's more of a reference to the "user" of the API, i.e. the application. One of the suggestions from @joerchan was actually APP. We can still reconsider this. I suggested CUSTOM since the stack has some existing built-in checks and this is about an additional one to be done by the user of the API.

> It's more of a reference to the "user" of the API, i.e. the application. One of the suggestions from @joerchan was actually APP. We can still reconsider this. I suggested CUSTOM since the stack has some existing built-in checks and this is about an additional one to be done by the user of the API.

So usually (with nRF5 SDK) we have referred to these things as "Application control of < feature >" when giving control over something that would normally be stack controlled. Examples of this are data length and phy.
Which is why I initially suggested APP, but I'd prefer to be consistent with other kconfigs as well.
I remember someone started to use "USER" for this, for example `/** Register user callback for HCI Vendor-Specific Events` and it's kconfig `CONFIG_BT_HCI_VS_EVT_USER`.
It seems it's not widely used, only other instance would be LVGL_MEM_POOL_USER that I could find.

So personally I would prefer APP because as @demantmrrv pointed out we want to distinguish in pairing from the "User input" i.e a person typing in the passkey and the application without user involvement.
Based on @joerchan, @jhedberg and @aescolar's comments I have pushed the latest changes now. RFC.

issue_context.title: Add SMP function similar to bt_conn_get_info
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It is desirable for the app to dynamically filter pairing requests on the `AuthReq` content, in this case the `Bonding_Flags`, to decide whether to accept or reject an attempt. It can be extended with information on IO Caps, OOB, Max Encryption Key Size and Key Distribution fields.
This feature request is a dynamic solution opposing the static proposal in [PR#21002](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/21002) and with optionally much more information.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add a function to the SMP API such as `bt_smp_get_pairing_info(const struct bt_conn *conn, struct bt_smp_pairing_info *info)` that returns information including, but not limited to, AuthReq parameters for a connection. It can also include the rest of the fields available during pairing.
It will be the callers responsibility to call this function at the right time e.g. during `pairing_confirm`. In case the SMP should not expose a public API it can be called from conn.c instead.
This feature can be implemented as an addition to the current API and is functionally non-intrusive.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Besides the static solution in [PR#21002](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/21002) there is currently no way for the app to detect this parameter.

Alternatively, for this particular case, the `pairing_confirm` callback could be extended with a bond_flag parameter similar to `pairing_complete`. This implies an API change.

Second alternative could be to add `void (*pairing_info)(struct bt_conn *conn, struct bt_conn_pairing_info *info)` to `bt_conn_auth_cb` providing additional information during `pairing_req`, `pairing_rsp` and `security_req`.
